subject: Sunstone Health - eval run spec & scoring alignment
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@sunstonehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Sunstone Health - eval run spec & scoring alignment

Hi Emily / Sunstone team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a scoped eval running on Redwood: 

Recap (from today)
- Goal: validate model fit for clinical note summarization + short-answer extraction for triage-specific intents.
- Success criteria: high clinical fidelity (no hallucinated facts), recall on critical fields (meds, allergies) > 0.90, and human-A/B preference for summaries vs. current baseline.

Recommended initial model candidates (we'll run these in parallel):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (fast, cost-effective baseline)
- Llama-2-13B (higher-quality candidate for longer-context notes)
- Quantized 13B variant (Q4) to test cost/latency tradeoffs — Redwood can auto-select best quantization profile for the workload.

What we need from Sunstone to start (action items)
1) Sample dataset: ~1k rows representative of the live traffic (anonymized if PHI is present). CSV or JSONL is fine; see format below.
2) Labeling / scoring guidance: for each row, what is the gold reference (summary text / label values) and which metrics matter (EM, token-level F1 for entities, human preference).
3) Regulatory constraints: confirm whether dataset will contain PHI and whether it must be processed inside a Private deployment or VPC (if yes, we’ll route to Private eval).
4) Target timeline: confirm preferred 2-week window for initial run and stakeholder for results review.

Proposed timeline
- Wed (Nov 1): Sunstone shares sample + scoring template
- Fri (Nov 3): Redwood stage the eval and run initial pass against 3 model candidates
- Following Tue (Nov 7): internal scoring and a short results deck + meeting to review.

Dataset format (preferred)
- CSV columns: id, raw_note, reference_summary, labels_json (optional), label_type ("summary" | "entity_extraction")
- If JSONL preferred: one JSON object per line with keys id, prompt, reference, metadata.

Attachments & links we will use
- We can accept an S3 link or upload to the Drive folder we created: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rSunstoneEvalDriveExample

Next steps for you
- Emily: please send a 1k sample + a filled scoring_template.xlsx (we attached a template in Drive) and indicate whether PHI is present.

If you want, Ben can provide a short example prompt set (3-5 prompts) and scoring script we run on Redwood.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the results review once we have the sample.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---

Note: attachments we expect (for planning): sunstone_sample_1000.csv, scoring_template.xlsx; if PHI is present we will coordinate Private eval with Legal & Security.

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching a small sample and the scoring worksheet (see attached). A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) PHI: the sample contains redacted PHI but our full production data will contain PHI. Security is a requirement; if possible we prefer the eval to run inside a Private deployment (VPC) or your on-prem option.
2) Scoring: we'd like a combined approach — automated entity F1 for specific fields (meds, allergies, diagnoses), ROUGE-L for summaries, plus a human spot-check (50 rows) for clinical hallucination. We have a short list of 6 critical fields.
3) Timeline: can we aim for the run next week? Our stakeholders want an initial pass in 7 business days.

Attachments:
- sunstone_sample_1000.csv (attached)
- scoring_template.xlsx (attached)

Thanks — Emily

Subject: Re: Sunstone Health - eval run spec & scoring alignment

Emily — thanks for the sample and the worksheet. I reviewed the CSV quickly and sketched out an eval playbook you can reuse. High-level steps and specifics below.

Eval setup (what Redwood needs)
- Storage: upload sample to S3 or the Drive folder (we can pull from either).
- File format: CSV with header row is easiest. Required columns we will use: id, raw_note, reference_summary, label_type. Optional columns: entity_annotations (JSON string), priority_flag.
- If you prefer JSONL (one document per line) that also works; please indicate which format in the upload.

Prompt set (example templates)
- Summarization: 
  "Prompt: You are a clinical summarization assistant. Summarize the following clinical note focusing on chief complaint, key findings, and next steps in 3-4 sentences. Note: do not hallucinate medication changes."
- Entity extraction: 
  "Prompt: From the note below, extract medication names and dosages. Return a JSON list of objects with fields {name, dose, frequency}."

Scoring rubric (automated + human)
- Summaries: ROUGE-L and a human fidelity score (0-3) where 3 = no hallucination and clinically actionable.
- Entities: token-level F1 for meds/allergies; consider span-level EM for exact matches. Target: F1 >= 0.90 on meds/allergies.
- Regression controls: we will run the eval against your current baseline model to measure deltas. If a model shows >5% drop in any critical metric, flag for human review.

Artifacts we'll provide
- scoring_template.xlsx (attached) with metric mapping and example computations.
- prompt_set.jsonl in Drive with 50 sample prompts (we'll seed with variations).
- scoring script (Python) that computes ROUGE-L, token-F1, and aggregates per-batch. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rSunstoneEvalDriveExample

Operational notes
- If the data contains PHI, we will schedule the eval inside your Private deployment region — security will coordinate with your team for access.
- Runtime: initial 1k run against three model candidates typically completes in 2-3 hours of GPU time; full scoring and deck takes ~48 hours.

Next steps
- Emily: confirm upload location and whether you want Redwood to provision a Private eval.
- Jordan: I’ll prepare the prompt_set and push the scoring script to the Drive folder.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
